sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The projected shot count sits right at the line, and a +130 under price leaves room. The case stays above break-even across the supplied sensitivity range and after the market blend. No material blocker is identified.
assessment.model_case: The projected mean barely clears 1.5 and the median is one shot, so the under needs zero or one shot. The main weakness is Parekh's unverified power-play role: a power-play quarterback assignment could push his shot volume above the projection. The rookie prior and shrinkage are doing real work on 52 games.
assessment.price_case: Main line 1.5 at +130 versus a model fair price near -121. The low end of the sensitivity range still beats the +130 break-even, and the market-blended figure still clears it. Only one other book is quoted, so this is not broad consensus.
assessment.context_case: The injury snapshot shows no listing for Parekh, but absence from the table is not clearance. Huberdeau's listed return date could reshape Calgary's power-play units. That effect is unknown and unverified.

qualitative_review.countercase: Parekh may be deployed as a high-volume power-play shooter, so the mean could sit well above 1.5. The rookie position prior may understate his shot rate. If Huberdeau's return does not displace him, two shots is a routine outcome. A single DraftKings quote at +130 may reflect a stale or soft line rather than value.

Check whether Huberdeau returns and how Calgary's power-play units are arranged.
Reconfirm +130 is still available before the 9:10 PM EST faceoff.

evidence.excerpt: Jonathan Huberdeau (C); Hip; IR. Expected to be out until at least Nov 2
evidence.interpretation: If Huberdeau returns tonight, Calgary's power-play and forward usage could shift, which may affect Parekh's opportunity in either direction. The listed date is not a guaranteed return.

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval

assessment.reason: The projected mean sits right at 2.5 and the median is two shots, so the +110 under clears break-even. The model's stale goalie mix weakens confidence in input freshness. Goalie identity matters little for a skater's shot volume, though, so it is not a material blocker.
assessment.model_case: Smith's projected volume is essentially equal to the line, and the under value comes from the shape of the count distribution rather than a low mean. The weakness is a thin margin: the low end of the sensitivity range is only slightly above break-even, so a modest bump in ice time or power-play usage could erase it.
assessment.price_case: Main line 2.5 at +110 versus a model fair price near -127. The market-blended figure only narrowly clears the +110 break-even. Only one other book is quoted.
assessment.context_case: The snapshot lists Cooley on IR, yet the model gives him the largest share of Calgary's starts. That conflict points to a stale goalie input, but the effect on shot counts is likely small. Wennberg's absence may already be reflected in recent games.

qualitative_review.countercase: Smith is San Jose's top-line center, and with Wennberg out his ice time and power-play time could run above the projected 17.9 minutes. A mean at the line leaves little cushion, and the thin sensitivity floor shows the edge disappears with modest extra usage. The stale goalie input suggests other features may also lag.
open_checks: Confirm Calgary's starting goalie; the model's goalie mix appears stale.
Check Smith's line and power-play deployment with Wennberg absent.
Reconfirm the +110 price before the 9:10 PM EST faceoff.
